findings.title: retryCount-based deleteMany drops the SMS method filter
findings.body: The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` branch of the deleteMany has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) condition, unlike the existing branch. Any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1 will be hard-deleted by this SMS cron endpoint. Today only this file increments retryCount, but the column is on the shared WorkflowReminder model and other flows (e.g. WhatsApp/email scheduling crons or future code) may use it; when they do, this cron will silently delete their pending reminders. The condition should be scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders.

findings.title: Retry counter incremented from stale in-memory value instead of atomic increment
findings.body: Both the failure path (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, computed from the value fetched at the start of the run. If two runs of this cron overlap (or a run is retried), increments are lost and a permanently failing reminder can be retried indefinitely, defeating the intended two-attempt limit. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

findings.title: Reminders skipped for missing message/sendTo never count a retry and never get cleaned up
findings.body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing (e.g. attendee has no SMS number), the code falls through without scheduling and without incrementing retryCount. Such a reminder stays `scheduled: false` and is re-fetched and re-skipped by every cron run until scheduledDate passes the 7-day window, wasting queries. Since this PR's stated goal is to stop endlessly reprocessing failing reminders, this skip path should also increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) so it is retired after two attempts.
